cases.name: lite rtti behaves correctly
cases.note: The executable Rust test preserves the pinned TypeId equality and inequality sequence, exact dynamic-cast success and null sequence, constructor values, and shared-ownership cast results through Rust's live Any, TypeId, Box, and Rc owners.

adaptation.rationale: Rust has no raw-pointer lite_rtti_cast or intrusive rcp cast surface; Any and TypeId own exact dynamic-type identity while Box and Rc own the corresponding unique and shared lifetimes without recreating the C++ macros.
adaptation.inapplicable_observable: The numeric CONST_ID hash, macro-generated liteTypeID method, raw base-pointer cast mechanics, and intrusive RefCnt bookkeeping are C++ implementation observables; the pinned test asserts only identity relationships, cast nullness or exact referent, constructor fields, and shared-cast success, all preserved by the Rust owners.

cases.name: truncated file import never crashes
cases.note: The executable Rust test imports every exact byte prefix of the pinned asset in order and drops every returned or partially-owned Rust value before the next prefix, including the empty and full prefixes.

adaptation.rationale: Rust File::import returns Result<File>, so a failed import cannot coexist with a non-null partially-built File and ownership cleanup occurs through Drop rather than a raw File pointer destructor.
adaptation.inapplicable_observable: The separate C++ ImportResult value, independently nullable File pointer, gNoOpFactory pointer, and allocator effect of deleting an uninitialized m_backboard are unrepresentable in the Rust Result ownership surface; the exact every-prefix import and safe destruction lifecycle remains executable.

cases.name: full file still imports after the guards
cases.note: The executable Rust test imports the exact full pinned asset after the prefix guard sweep and observes a retained default artboard through the live File owner.

adaptation.rationale: Rust expresses successful file import as Result<File> and artboard presence as Option rather than the C++ ReadRiveFile helper's owning and raw pointers.
adaptation.inapplicable_observable: C++ raw File and Artboard pointer non-nullness and the ReadRiveFile helper's pointer ownership are not exposed by Rust; successful Result construction and Some(default_artboard) preserve the pinned success and artboard-presence observations.

cases.name: ieee_float_divide
cases.note: The executable Rust test preserves every pinned operand and result assertion, including the source's integer -0 spelling, infinities, zero results, repeated infinite division, and NaN classifications through primitive IEEE f32 division.

adaptation.rationale: The upstream math::ieee_float_divide helper is a C++ portability wrapper for IEEE division; Rust f32 division is the language-owned IEEE operation and needs no runtime wrapper.
adaptation.inapplicable_observable: Calling the specifically named C++ inline math::ieee_float_divide wrapper is not a Rust runtime observable; every numeric equality, sign, infinity, zero, and NaN result asserted by the pinned body is preserved.

cases.name: bit_cast
cases.note: The executable Rust test preserves all five pinned bit patterns and their exact positive, negative, infinite, and NaN f32 observations through f32::from_bits.

adaptation.rationale: Rust f32::from_bits is the language-owned bit reinterpretation operation corresponding to the C++ math::bit_cast<float> portability template.
adaptation.inapplicable_observable: The C++ math::bit_cast<float> template instantiation and its internal representation-copy mechanism have no Rust call identity; the exact input bits and resulting f32 observations remain executable.

cases.name: clamp_cast
cases.note: The executable Rust test preserves all eight pinned source values, destination widths and signedness, clamped boundaries, and exact integer results through Rust primitive min and clamp owners.

adaptation.rationale: The upstream math::clamp_cast overload set is a C++ template and integral-promotion portability surface; Rust primitive min, clamp, and explicit casts own the corresponding typed operations.
adaptation.inapplicable_observable: C++ template overload selection and implicit integral-promotion mechanics are not Rust observables; each pinned source value, destination type boundary, and clamped result is asserted explicitly.

cases.name: clz
cases.note: The executable Rust test preserves the 32-bit and 64-bit boundary assertions, every loop iteration, one libc rand sample per iteration, and both leading-zero assertions through the primitive leading_zeros owner.

adaptation.rationale: The C++ math::clz32 and math::clz64 functions are portability wrappers over platform leading-zero operations; Rust integer leading_zeros is the language-owned operation and libc::rand preserves the pinned random-sample action.
adaptation.inapplicable_observable: The named C++ clz32/clz64 wrapper dispatch and compiler-builtin selection are not observable in Rust; bit widths, loop bounds, random-mask construction, and every expected leading-zero count remain asserted.

cases.name: rotateleft32
cases.note: The executable Rust test preserves both pinned u32 inputs, rotation counts, and exact hexadecimal results through u32::rotate_left.

adaptation.rationale: The upstream math::rotateleft32 function is a C++ portability wrapper; Rust u32::rotate_left is the language-owned 32-bit rotate operation.
adaptation.inapplicable_observable: Invocation of the specifically named C++ rotateleft32 wrapper and its platform intrinsic dispatch is not a Rust observable; both input/count/result triples are preserved exactly.

cases.name: msb
cases.note: The executable Rust test preserves the exact zero-through-nine assertions, all 29 shifted-ten assertions, and the all-bits-set terminal assertion through the primitive leading_zeros owner.

adaptation.rationale: The upstream math::msb helper derives the one-based most-significant-bit position from a leading-zero count; Rust exposes the language-owned u32::BITS and leading_zeros operations directly.
adaptation.inapplicable_observable: The named C++ math::msb helper call is not a Rust observable; the same one-based result expression and every pinned input/result assertion remain executable.

cases.name: positive_mod
cases.note: The executable Rust test preserves the pinned fixture, action order, concrete runtime owner, and assertions.
